name: 誠鮨
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田駿河台4-3 新お茶の水ビル B1F
cuisine: An Edomae sushi counter that has been in the basement of the Shin-Ochanomizu Building since 1981, doing the slow work — simmering, curing, marinating — rather than just slicing. Lunch is a limited-run 特選ちらし at ¥1,300; nigiri sets run ¥3,500 (上) and ¥4,500 (特上) with a soup, おまかせ nigiri ¥6,000, and the 誠 course from ¥12,000 including a drink.
neighborhood: Kanda-Surugadai 4-chōme — one minute from JR Ochanomizu's Hijiribashi exit (Chūō-Sōbu line) and one minute from Shin-Ochanomizu (Tokyo Metro Chiyoda line), which is exactly where the light record placed it; 6 minutes from Ochanomizu on the Marunouchi line. The shop is in the basement of the Shin-Ochanomizu Building, 114 m from the station.
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim, no allergen information, and two specific things on this counter make wheat likelier than a diner might assume. First, the shop is proud of exactly the preparations that carry it: it describes doing 「煮る」「締める」「漬け込む」 Edomae work on the fish, and it singles out its かんぴょう — simmered gourd, cooked in soy sauce and mirin — as a house specialty alongside the ガリ. Second, its shari is 「数種類のお酢をオリジナルの配合でブレンド」, a proprietary blend of several vinegars, which is precisely the kind of detail that cannot be assumed wheat-free without asking, since grain vinegars in Japan may be wheat-derived. Nikiri brushed onto nigiri is wheat shōyu unless stated otherwise. Against that, this is a counter with a chef in front of you and a menu that says outright 「ご予算に応じて調理致します」 — they will build to request — so a wheat-avoiding diner has somewhere to start. Ask about the shari blend and the nikiri specifically, and expect the kanpyō and any simmered anago to be off the table.
vegan_detail: An Edomae sushi-ya whose entire identity is fish. Tabelog records 魚料理にこだわる; the course structure runs 先付け・刺身・焼物・煮物・寿司・お椀・デザート and the お椀 will be a katsuo or kombu-and-katsuo dashi. There is no vegetable course and no plant-based option advertised.

roles: 大将・店主 (owner-chef; not named on the shop's site)
chef_bio.origin: Kanda-Surugadai, Chiyoda-ku — the shop has never moved from the Shin-Ochanomizu Building basement
chef_bio.background: 誠鮨 opened in 1981 (昭和56年) in the basement of the 新お茶の水ビル and has traded there ever since, describing itself as 「地元に愛されて」 — a neighbourhood shop for the offices and hospitals of Surugadai rather than a destination. Its stated principle is a pun on its own name: 「誠実であること」を大切に, keeping faith, applied to the sushi, the room and the service. The kitchen leans on the unglamorous half of Edomae technique — the fish is simmered, cured or marinated over time rather than simply cut, and the shop makes a point that its ガリ and かんぴょう are made in-house with as much care as the fish. The rice is its other claim: a proprietary blend of several vinegars, aimed at a soft mouthfeel that lifts the seafood, and the shari is re-cut twice a day so it is served at the right temperature. The room is dressed seasonally, with craft pieces changed for occasions like Momo-no-sekku and Tango-no-sekku. It seats 24 — a ten-seat counter plus tables — takes reservations, accepts all the major cards, and can be hired for parties of up to fifty. The menu is printed in Japanese and English. Tabelog rates it 3.34, with a dinner spend of ¥10,000–¥14,999 against a ¥1,000–¥1,999 lunch.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「誠実であること」 — to be sincere; the shop takes its name as its instruction.
chef_bio.specialty: The lunch-only 特選ちらし at ¥1,300, made in limited numbers and changed with the season; おまかせ寿司 at ¥6,000; the 誠 course from ¥12,000. In-house ガリ and かんぴょう are named by the shop as points of pride.

anecdotes.text: The shop cuts its sushi rice twice a day rather than once, purely so that it reaches the customer at the right temperature.
It sells the side dishes as hard as the fish: 「鮨屋の華である、鮮度のよい厳選した鮨ネタはもちろん自慢ですが、ガリやかんぴょうなど、手間を惜しまず拵えた副菜も当店の自慢です」.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13025203 lists 誠鮨 under 御茶ノ水/寿司 at 東京都千代田区神田駿河台4-3 新お茶の水ビルB1F, tel 03-3295-8537, coordinates 35.69882/139.76507, 1 minute from JR Ochanomizu's Hijiribashi exit and 1 minute from Shin-Ochanomizu (114 m), weekday hours 11:30–14:00 and 17:00–21:30 L.O. closed Sundays and public holidays, 24 seats (10 counter, plus tables), reservations accepted, VISA/Master/JCB/AMEX/Diners, all non-smoking, private hire up to 50, 日本酒あり and 魚料理にこだわる, an opening year of 1981, and a 3.34 rating. The shop's own site makoto-sushi.jp confirms the 昭和56年 founding in the same basement, the 「誠実であること」 principle, the multi-vinegar shari blend cut twice daily, the in-house ガリ and かんぴょう, and the 煮る/締める/漬け込む Edomae work; its お品書き page gives the full bilingual price list — 上にぎり ¥3,500, 特上にぎり ¥4,500, 上ちらし ¥3,500, 特上ちらし ¥4,500, おまかせ寿司 ¥6,000, the 誠 course from ¥12,000 with a beer or soft drink included, and the lunch-only 特選ちらし at ¥1,300 in limited numbers.

gf_cross_contamination.text: No allergen information is published anywhere on the shop's site or its Tabelog page, and no gluten-free preparation is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop's named side specialty かんぴょう is a soy-sauce-simmered preparation, and it describes 煮る and 漬け込む as core to its Edomae work — all standard wheat-shōyu constructions. No tamari is mentioned.
The shari is a proprietary blend of several vinegars — 「数種類のお酢をオリジナルの配合でブレンド」 — whose composition is not published, so it cannot be assumed free of grain-derived vinegar.

vegan_cross_contact.text: An Edomae sushi counter; Tabelog records 魚料理にこだわる and the course runs through sashimi, grilled, simmered, sushi and a soup course. No plant-based option exists.

staff_allergy_handling.text: The shop states on its menu page that it will cook to the customer's budget and requirements — 「その他、ご予算に応じて調理致します」 / 'We can arrange the menu on your budget' — which is an opening for a dietary request made at reservation, though nothing about allergies is promised.

positives.text: The menu is published in Japanese and English, so a non-Japanese-speaking diner can at least read what is being offered before asking about it.

cultural_comfort.level: Unusually approachable for an Edomae counter
cultural_comfort.note: One minute from Ochanomizu's Hijiribashi exit and one from Shin-Ochanomizu, but it is in a basement — go down into the Shin-Ochanomizu Building rather than looking for a street frontage. The menu is bilingual Japanese/English with prices tax-included, which removes most of the anxiety of a sushi counter; there are tables as well as the ten-seat counter, children are welcomed at every age, and all the major cards are accepted. Lunch is the low-risk way in: the ¥1,300 特選ちらし is made in limited numbers, so go early in the 11:30–14:00 window. Closed Sundays and public holidays. Reservations on 03-3295-8537; the shop says it will build a menu to your budget, which is also the right moment to raise a dietary restriction. It has been here since 1981 and reads as a local office-district shop, not a tourist one.

enrich_note: Confirmed. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for 誠鮨 (HTTP 200, 48件) returns eight restaurants with that exact name across Japan — Hokkaidō (two), Kanagawa, Gunma, Aomori, Tochigi and Tokyo — and exactly one in Tokyo: 13025203 at 神田駿河台4-3 新お茶の水ビルB1F, one minute from 新御茶ノ水駅, which is precisely the station the light record names, with the genre 寿司 matching the sweep's 江戸前寿司. The shop's own site makoto-sushi.jp independently confirms the address, the basement location and the 1981 founding, and describes the sushi as 江戸前 in its own page title. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.698822, 139.765075), about 40 m from the sweep's approximate pin. gf_confidence stays at the light record's 'ask' but the detail is now evidenced rather than assumed — the shop's own copy names kanpyō and long simmering/curing work, and describes an undisclosed multi-vinegar shari blend.
